skill.name: debugger
skill.description: Diagnoses errors, failing tests, and unexpected behavior through reproducible investigation, root cause analysis, minimal fixes, and verification.
skill.summary: Find root causes and verify focused fixes for software failures.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Software failures can hide behind incomplete logs and unclear reproduction steps. This skill structures investigation, isolates root causes, proposes minimal fixes, and defines verification.
actual_capabilities: Captures error messages, stack traces, constraints, and reproduction steps.
Isolates likely failure locations from logs, recent changes, and variable states.
Forms testable hypotheses and identifies evidence needed to confirm each one.
Recommends strategic logging and focused experiments for difficult failures.
Proposes minimal fixes with verification tests and prevention recommendations.
limitations: Diagnosis quality depends on accurate errors, logs, changes, and reproduction details.
The skill does not replace testing in the affected environment.
It cannot inspect repositories, services, or runtime state without access.
It requires clarification when permissions, safety boundaries, or success criteria are missing.

use_cases.title: Resolve Application Errors
use_cases.description: Trace an exception from its stack trace and recent changes, then define a focused fix and regression test.

use_cases.title: Investigate Failing Tests
use_cases.description: Separate test defects from product defects by reproducing failures and checking assumptions, fixtures, and environment differences.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Production Incidents
use_cases.description: Use logs and observed symptoms to rank hypotheses, isolate affected components, and plan safe verification.

prompt_templates.title: Triage an Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this error message: [error]. Ask for missing context, identify likely failure areas, and give the first three checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a new error

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Failing Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate this failing test using [test output] and [recent changes]. Define reproduction steps, rank hypotheses, and suggest evidence for each.
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured investigation of a repeatable test failure

prompt_templates.title: Isolate an Intermittent Defect
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an isolation plan for this intermittent failure: [symptoms]. Include targeted logging, variable states, controlled experiments, and success criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced investigation when failures are inconsistent

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Root Cause Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [stack trace], [logs], [reproduction], and [diff]. Explain the root cause, propose the smallest fix, and define verification and prevention measures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Comprehensive diagnosis with available technical evidence

output_examples.input: A checkout test starts timing out after a client dependency update.
output: Root cause: The updated client waits for a callback that the test double never invokes.
Evidence: The failure begins after the update and stops at the callback wait.
Fix: Update the test double to match the current callback behavior.
Verification: Repeat the targeted test, then run the related checkout suite.

output_examples.input: A production service returns occasional unauthorized responses after token refresh.
output: Leading hypothesis: Concurrent requests reuse an expired token during refresh.
Evidence needed: Compare token timestamps, refresh events, and request identifiers.
Isolation plan: Add focused logging around token selection and refresh completion.
Verification: Reproduce concurrent requests and confirm every request uses the refreshed token.

best_practices: Provide the complete error, stack trace, reproduction steps, and recent relevant changes.
Test one hypothesis at a time and record evidence that confirms or rejects it.
Verify the fix with a targeted regression test and related test coverage.
anti_patterns: Do not change several components before identifying the failure location.
Do not suppress errors or symptoms without explaining the underlying cause.
Do not accept a fix until the original failure is reproducible and verified.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the full error, stack trace, reproduction steps, expected behavior, actual behavior, environment details, and recent changes.

faq.question: Can this skill debug intermittent failures?
faq.answer: Yes. It can design logging and controlled experiments, but intermittent issues require enough observations to compare successful and failed runs.

faq.question: Will it modify my code automatically?
faq.answer: It can propose or implement a focused fix when tools and permissions allow. You should still review and test every change.

faq.question: Can it diagnose production incidents?
faq.answer: Yes, when you provide relevant logs, symptoms, timelines, and constraints. Validate all recommendations through your incident procedures.

faq.question: How does it verify a root cause?
faq.answer: It links the diagnosis to evidence, tests competing hypotheses, reproduces the failure, and confirms that a focused change removes it.

faq.question: When should I use another skill?
faq.answer: Use another skill when the task primarily requires security analysis, architecture design, deployment operations, or specialized domain knowledge.
